subject: Information Theory
title: TLS and HTTPS
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on TLS and HTTPS.

hook.text: Every time you see the padlock icon in your browser, dozens of cryptographic operations execute in milliseconds.

buildup.text: TLS negotiates a shared key, verifies the server's identity, and encrypts everything—all before the page loads.

discovery.text: The handshake uses public-key crypto for key exchange, then switches to fast symmetric encryption for data.

twist.text: TLS 1.3 trimmed the handshake to a single round trip. Faster and more secure than all previous versions.

climax.text: Over 95% of web traffic is now encrypted. TLS turned cryptography from military tech into daily infrastructure.

punchline.text: That padlock? Decades of math, in milliseconds.

quiz.question: What does TLS do during the handshake?
options: Negotiates encryption keys and verifies the server
